1.7: Exponent and radical laws follow from positive-base real powers; positive bases exclude even-root and complex-branch sign errors. Polynomial squares checked by multiplication.

2.23: Hydrostatic pressure follows dp/dh=rho*g, buoyancy displaced-fluid weight; specific/molar volumes and specific weight use distinct mass, amount and force bases. Pa/bar factors checked with NIST SI.

2.27: Latent heat sign is heat absorbed, Snell/lens relations use declared normal and image conventions, signed height magnification is -v/u. Beat magnitude is distinct from signed Doppler shift.

3.30: Signed planar equilibrium and linear spring magnitudes are explicit. Wire arc centroid follows first-moment integration; triangular/trapezoidal area centroid origins are stated.

3.33: Pitch/module relations and Willis planetary relation checked with signed speeds. Fixed ring/carrier cases correctly distinguish carrier speed and planet spin.
3.34: Ideal pulley travel and effort follow work balance and supporting-part count. Differential pulley derives travel pi*(R-r) per turn. Weighted tension sums are conditional recurrences, not calibrated universal sheave efficiencies.
3.35: Screw/worm expressions checked through work per turn and speed ratio. Additive screw friction is explicitly approximate and does not replace exact helix friction equations.

3.37: Constant-acceleration identities use signed axes. Projectile range and maximum height are separated from time-dependent position; equal landing height is required for range.
3.38: Angular constant-acceleration formulas and work/energy/power follow time integration. Oblique work, datum height and same signed torque/speed axis are explicit.
3.39: Fixed-axis rotational inertia and torque are consistent; centripetal force is a net-force component. Pendulum expressions are small-angle periods with inertia about the pivot.
3.40: Mass moments checked by radial/length integration. Plate axes lie in its plane; thin-wall, solid sphere and centred rod are distinct geometries. Conical pendulum angle is measured from vertical.
3.41: Parallel-axis theorem requires a centroid reference. Collision momentum and restitution are independent constraints with one signed axis; energy loss uses initial minus final translation.

3.44: Composite sections require disjoint areas or overlap subtraction and coincident centroid axes. Added rectangle formula is explicitly restricted, not a generic cross/T/U profile expression.
3.45: Beam reaction balance and Euler-Bernoulli integration confirm load/UDL deflections/slopes. Point-load deflection is not generally maximum. Normalized beta coordinates and reflected location branch are correct.
3.46: Circular-shaft torsion uses polar J and Wp=J/r; radians and rpm-to-second power conversion checked. Noncircular sections require another torsion model.
3.47: Euler buckling follows eigenvalue boundary conditions; least-axis inertia and slender-elastic limitations explicit. Fixed/pinned factor 0.6991556596 is approximate; safety arithmetic is not code approval.

4.53: Bearing heat balance conserves power; manufacturer's X/Y load factors remain external inputs. Basic L10 exponent is 3 for balls and 10/3 for rollers; revolutions/hour/rpm scaling checked against SKF rating-life definition.
4.54: Elastic circular torsion and engineering shear strain distinguished from total twist; von Mises combines one normal and one shear stress at the same physical point.

5.55: Mass number counts nucleons and is not an atomic mass.

5.59: Alpha, beta-minus, beta-plus, electron-capture and gamma changes conserve charge/nucleon count with required neutrinos and physically allowed transition conditions.

5.62: Redox electron direction and oxidation-number sums conserve formal charge; actual species require a balanced chemical reaction.
5.63: Atomic mass unit is one twelfth of a specified free neutral ground-state carbon-12 atom; kilogram conversion is not exact.
5.64: Amount/count, final-solution molarity, mass fraction and dilution conserve the explicitly chosen substance and units; no reaction/loss is assumed.

6.79: Charge, resistance/resistivity and conductance identities preserve the correct dimensions and fixed-temperature linear model. Positive temperature rise uses +alpha*dT. Node currents are signed.

6.81: Delta-star node pairing checked by equivalent pair resistances. DC/RMS resistor energy and two-conductor cable length conventions are consistent.
6.82: Wheatstone zero-detector-current relation, n-1 interplate capacitors, capacitor energy and RC step derive from node charge/energy. Thermal efficiency is retained energy fraction.
6.83: RC discharge and series/parallel capacitance follow charge conservation. Coulomb force is a magnitude; field F/q is signed, so the magnitude condition was clarified to positive q or absolute values.

6.85: Reluctance flux, one-air-gap stress, Lorentz force and Faraday-Lenz signs checked with declared orientation. Back emf is distinct from passive terminal inductor voltage.

6.89: Parallel branch admittance is G+jB, with B positive capacitive. True/displacement power factors coincide only for sinusoidal excitation.

6.93: Balanced cable drops/losses use per-phase impedance and total three-phase power. Short-circuit per-unit ratios share voltage and power bases; IEC factors and protective decisions are excluded.
6.94: Thevenin three-phase fault relation and line-line ratio require sequence assumptions. Peak factor depends on X/R and fault timing; no universal range is asserted.
6.95: DC machine constants include the chosen rev/s basis. AC synchronous speed uses pole pairs; rotor electrical frequency is |slip|f, including generating slip.
6.96: Four-band resistor arithmetic yields numeric ohms from separately identified digits/multiplier; colour interpretation is external.
6.97: Capacitor digit/multiplier arithmetic yields numeric picofarads, not farads; actual marking scheme remains manufacturer-specific.

7.102: BJT alpha/beta conversion follows emitter current balance; AC/DC operating-point and leakage definitions are distinct.
7.103: Gain magnitudes deliberately omit inversion sign; ideal BJT gm=Ic/VT and parallel collector/load model are bias-limited.
7.104: Negative-feedback reduction uses stable loop gain; gain-bandwidth and distortion expressions are approximations. Series capacitor equivalent is not silently applied to shunt/Miller capacitances.

7.106: Class-A transformer and single-supply class-B formulas use different rail/swing definitions. Class-B power and each-transistor maximum loss checked by half-cycle current integration.
7.107: THD excludes fundamental/DC; inverting amplifier gain follows summing-node KCL within linear op-amp operation.
7.108: Noninverting/differential/summing amplifier relations require matching resistor ratios and negative feedback; unity follower requires unity-gain stability.
7.109: Source circuit reread. Node equations give Zin=R1(1+sR2C)/(1+sR1C); exact frequency-specific series L and Q replace overgeneralized approximations. Howland current sign follows the drawn node and ratio matching.
7.110: Source circuit reread. Multiplier Zin=R1R2/(R1+R2)+1/[sC(1+R2/R1)] gives the exact multiplied capacitance and corrected loss tangent omega*C*R2. Sallen-Key and equal-C MFB filter scaling checked from ideal nodal equations.
7.111: Source circuit reread. Full two-node analysis confirms equal-C notch resistor proportions, pole Q and nonunity passband gain 2Q²/(1+2Q²). All-pass needs factor 2, Wien period needs a square root; their earlier corrections are retained.

7.115: Antilog diode polarity, negative weighted-DAC output and one-shot exponential timing use explicit rail/reference conventions.
7.116: Series RLC Q/voltage magnification and half-power bandwidth are resonance relations. Lossy parallel-coil resistance L/(CRs) follows cancellation of input susceptance.
7.117: High-Q circulating current is approximate. Constant-k T/pi prototypes use their declared half/double component parameters; nominal image impedance is not general input impedance.
7.118: Power dB is 10log; unequal real resistances add the proper voltage/current correction. AM envelope expression excludes overmodulation; FM beta uses peak frequency deviation.
7.119: Logic gates use Boolean operators; base expansion uses bounded integer digits, not analog algebra.
7.121: All Boolean identities confirmed by complete A/B/C truth tables; distributivity, absorption and De Morgan statements are consistent.

8.122: Rectifier averages checked by direct integration of one, two, three and six ideal sinusoidal conduction envelopes with phase/line RMS clearly distinguished.
8.123: Ripple RMS removes the squared DC component from total RMS; RL ripple transfer is frequency-specific.
8.124: LC high-frequency and capacitor-input ripple are limited approximations; AC RMS ripple is not peak-to-peak.
8.125: LC and RC-loaded ripple transfers follow impedances at the actual harmonic; DC divider estimate neglects charging ripple.
8.126: Half-wave capacitor peak ripple and PIV use one charging event per line period and ideal diode limits.
8.127: Full-wave capacitor ripple uses twice the charging frequency; centre-tap PIV uses one half-winding peak.
8.128: All waveform/phase-cut means and RMS values checked by integrating over the complete period. Conduction beta=pi-alpha and pulse count explain the factors 2 and required RMS square roots.
8.129: Thermal resistance rise is steady-state; series thermal resistances require one dominant path. Half-wave controlled mean follows the conduction integral.
8.130: Freewheeling and resistive versus continuous-current controlled bridges have different conduction intervals. Inversion requires an active DC source.

9.134: Otto cycle efficiency and gas compression follow reversible air-standard and polytropic models; effective port-closure ratio is geometric, not a trapping model.
9.135: Diesel cycle cutoff efficiency follows constant-pressure heat addition with 1<cutoff<compression ratio. Fuel efficiency uses lower heating value and SI-specific consumption.

9.137: Four-stroke MEP power has factor 1/2; charge/combustion MEP relation follows trapped air and fuel energy using the same swept-volume reference.
9.138: Torque/rev-s and mean piston speed factors checked. Oxygen mass demand follows C/H/S elemental balances; oxygen air mole fraction is not oxygen mass fraction.
9.139: Delivered versus retained air and cycle rate are separate; mass flow from brake power uses kg/J consumption.
9.140: Hydrocarbon combustion conserves C/H/O/N and the dry product mole fractions sum to one for lambda>=1. Approximate binary dry air neglects argon and dissociation.
9.141: Air-delivery/trapping/scavenging identities follow explicit mass partitions. Compressor/turbine isentropic efficiency use matching outlet pressure.
9.142: Slider-crank expansion and its time derivatives use constant omega; dead-centre accelerations agree with exact geometry. Inertia reaction opposes acceleration and gas force uses differential pressure.
9.143: Crank-angle mean force produces mean work/torque; rotating and reciprocating mass models are explicitly approximations.
9.144: Primary/secondary excitation and chosen half-primary counterbalance are not universal optimal balance. Free-free torsional mode excludes rigid-body rotation; rpm/order conversions are explicit.

9.146: Pitch slip and cube laws are conditional propulsion approximations; Admiralty constant has unit-dependent dimensions. Heat flux is distinct from heat rate.
9.147: Series thermal resistances use one area basis. Cooling-water flow follows fuel heat fraction, not a brake-power fraction.
9.148: Cooler energy balance and LMTD include its equal-temperature-difference limit; hydraulic power uses strictly positive efficiency.

10.149: Saturated mixture mass quality interpolates h and v, not volume quality. Superheat starts from saturated vapour hg and uses an interval cp estimate.
10.150: Boiler efficiency is a control-volume enthalpy balance with declared inlet/outlet numbering; all spray/blowdown/steam flows must be consistently included.
10.151: Turbine isentropic efficiency and simplified cycle efficiency have distinct pump/auxiliary exclusions. Nozzle speed follows steady-flow energy with J/kg versus numeric kJ/kg conversion.
10.152: Jet/nozzle/blade/exit energy losses are specific ideal impulse-stage bookkeeping, not all reaction stages. Velocity triangle uses vector differences and angle-branch selection.
10.153: Euler work uses signed swirl and inlet/outlet blade speed. Reaction ratio needs equal stage inlet/outlet kinetic energy for Euler work to equal the stage static enthalpy drop; the condition was made explicit.

11.155: Closed-system energy sign and cyclic efficiency are distinct. Entropy Qrev/T requires reversible isothermal transfer; Carnot limits use kelvin. Humid-air pressure and humidity ratio use ideal partial pressures.
11.156: Moist-air enthalpy is per kg dry air, with common zero datum. Water injection/mixing conserve dry air, vapour mass and enthalpy; complete evaporation must be feasible. Gas mixture R and molar mass use mass fractions.

11.159: Molecular mass, Avogadro and gas constants use consistent molar units. Nu/Re/Pe/Pr/St definitions distinguish thermal diffusivity, kinematic viscosity and film coefficient.
11.160: Polytropic formulas derive from pV^n plus ideal-gas law and first law. n=1 is a separate reversible isothermal work limit. Equal-temperature endpoint entropy needs T2=T1 even for irreversible paths; missing individual qualifications corrected.
11.161: Source reread. Emitted radiation is not net radiation. Sieder-Tate fits are empirical, geometry/property/entrance limits apply; the damaged printed turbulent length condition remains explicitly unresolved.
11.162: Dittus-Boelter uses smooth developed turbulent tube flow and different heated/cooled Pr exponents; source-specific range is retained without claiming calibration for other fluids.
11.163: Source reread. Vertical plate and horizontal-cylinder fit geometry/length were missing locally and are now explicit. Legacy 1.13 condensation coefficient lacks established smooth-film calibration and remains open; 0.725 horizontal-tube law has a separate draining-film model.
11.164: Rayleigh denominator is nu*alpha, not nu^2, and film absolute temperature is arithmetic mean. Morgan/McAdams coefficients must come from matching geometry/range; they are external fit parameters.
11.165: Vertical-plate power-law and Churchill-Chu correlations are empirical heat-transfer models with specified Rayleigh ranges and positive Pr.
11.166: Gray-surface radiation assumes full enclosure/view factor one. Supply temperature effectiveness is not total enthalpy effectiveness. Degree-day heating energy needs 24 hours/day.
11.167: Mass continuity and incompressible volume continuity have distinct density assumptions; nu=mu/rho at the same state.
11.168: Hydraulic diameter uses wetted perimeter. Bernoulli is a streamline energy balance without losses/shaft work and with consistent static pressure and height datum.
11.169: Loss-inclusive head balance, total hydraulic power and NPSHa use defined total/static/absolute pressure bases. Affinity laws require similar operating points and distinguish scaling from impeller trimming; specific speed is unit-dependent.
11.170: Ideal-gas density/reference-volume scaling keeps absolute p/T and composition fixed; low-Mach fan pressure/power scaling assumes fixed volume point. Discharge coefficient includes contraction as well as velocity.

11.174: Sudden expansion coefficient follows momentum and energy; sharp-contraction coefficient is only a geometry-specific empirical approximation.
11.176: Series flow conserves one mass rate, parallel mass rates sum, and parallel branch total head differences share endpoints; raw friction losses need not match with different gains.

13.185: Compass/deviation/variation signs follow east-positive correction, with deviation evaluated at actual compass heading and no hidden cardinal-case signs.
13.186: Signed latitude increment excludes pole crossing.

14.195: Density conversion is at fixed geometry; physical vessel mass does not change merely with water density. TPC scales directly, MCT scaling is hydrostatic-dominated approximation.
14.196: Loaded/discharged/shifted centres follow mass-first-moment conservation; free-surface correction uses liquid density times transverse surface second moment divided by displacement.
14.197: Displacement coefficients and rectangular waterplane inertia are geometry-specific. Density draft correction uses virtual reference-table mass and local TPC, not changing vessel mass.
14.198: Small-angle GM/GZ and roll period retain model limits. KN-KGsin(heel) alone requires centreline TCG, now explicit. Pendulum tangent uses the fixed measuring-plane separation, not the slanted wire length.
14.199: An onboard lifted weight keeps displacement fixed but moves effective centre to hook; restoring slope must select a stable equilibrium. Inverse formula follows the same signed moments.
14.200: A newly suspended external load adds mass and hook moments; KN changes with trial displacement, so inverse load is implicit.
14.201: Onboard load/counterweight shifts conserve total mass and adjust transverse moments with opposite signs; inverse assumes no counterweight vertical change.
14.202: Onboard lift plus newly added counterweight includes the counterweight vertical moment. The separately labelled inverse case is an already-onboard horizontally shifted counterweight, not the added-mass case.
14.203: Small-angle net transverse moment and full restoring balance are separate; adding counterweight changes displacement and vertical moment, including z_c.
14.204: New suspended load plus shifted onboard counterweight adds only the new load mass; inverse explicitly assumes no vertical shift of the counterweight.
14.205: Two new masses contribute both vertical moments, with counterweight lateral sign opposite load; hydrostatics update to total new mass.
14.206: Small-angle two-new-mass equation and exact lever equilibrium share a common sign system; inverse counterweight denominator uses trial KN and requires iteration/positive masses.
14.207: Rectangular heel draft envelope is illustrative only. MCT tonnes-metres/centimetre has factor 100, and GML approximation is separated from longitudinal BM.

14.210: LCF draft relation and first trim displacement correction use a straight waterline and explicit cm/metre factor. Hog/sag quarter-mean is empirical, not exact hull integration.
14.211: Reference volume and actual density conserve liquid mass; VCF must match authorized fluid/reference class. GOV/free water/OBQ distinctions prevent duplicate inventory subtraction.
14.212: Volumetric ullage is distinct from ullage height. Historical grain effective-GM and heeling-moment shortcuts remain unresolved without an approved grain geometry/procedure; small-angle heel alone is not Grain Code acceptance.
14.213: Ground reaction is a tonne-equivalent until multiplied by 1000g; local draft/trim estimates and apparent KG loss assume keel support and simplified hydrostatics, not general refloating approval.
14.214: Hull shear integrates signed net distributed load and moment integrates shear with stated end values. Half-hull moments use compatible force or tonne-force units and the correct aft arm.
14.217: Lightship/cargo weight moments must not double-subtract buoyancy. Wind force uses relative speed and drag coefficient/projected area, not an unexplained pressure shortcut.
14.218: One-line tension is a component projection, not multi-line mooring equilibrium. Simpson area/centroid moments use even panels, common spacing, signed stations and full-width convention.

15.219: Real/escalation rates use multiplicative purchasing-power factors, all per period. Annuity NPV and discounted payback follow geometric sums with a separate zero-rate limit; net NPV ratio is not gross profitability index.
15.220: Capital recovery/loan annuity are inverses of present-value factors, with zero-rate limits. Equal-principal payment uses previous balance; nominal annual/m conversion is not effective annual conversion.

16.223: Perpendicular/end/midship/LCF drafts are distinct. The historical one-third deflection correction remains an unvalidated empirical alternative to quarter-mean, with its sign applied once.
